bounds: Fees can reduce what a company receives or what an investor ultimately keeps.
Depending on the offering, there may be a platform fee, payment-processing charge, administrative fee, fund expense, or other disclosed cost.
The issuer may pay some fees, while an investor may pay others.
Do not assume one fee model applies to every offering.
Read the fee table, subscription documents, and payment screen, and distinguish a fee charged on top of your investment from one deducted from it.
In a fictional example, a $1,000 commitment with a 3% investor fee plus a $1 fixed charge would add $31, making the payment $1,031.
If instead the same charges were deducted from the $1,000, the amount reaching the investment would be $969.
The exact calculation depends on the documents.
Ask whether any ongoing costs apply after the offering closes and whether a fee is refundable if the raise fails or is cancelled.
